summary: The analyzed features demonstrate a high prevalence of treatment-effect modification. Radiographic features (304) and specific patient factors (302, 306) act as dual confounders and modifiers. Serum markers exhibit a split: creatinine (299) is a powerful treatment predictor with limited confounding utility but clear effect modification, while potassium (300) acts purely as an effect modifier. Smoking status indicators (306, 307) consistently signal confounding and modification, with cessation duration providing the strongest evidence.
